one_liner: Pumble has a free, self-serve REST API (API-key addon plus OAuth2 app SDK) and an official hosted MCP server. A toolkit is buildable now.
auth_notes: Pumble apps use an OAuth2 authorization-code flow (consent screen, code exchange with clientSecret); requests also need an x-app-token header. The simpler API Keys addon gives a static bearer key with a narrower API. Creating an app is self-serve through Configure apps.
access_notes: The API addon is available on all plans, including Free. Free plan allows three apps/integrations. An admin or member must be allowed to install apps in the workspace.
blocker_notes: Minor: the OAuth app requires a public HTTP server for events, and the API key addon has limited endpoints. Neither blocks a toolkit.

evidence.quote: Pumble uses OAuth2 in order to allow your app to access the API.
you must first generate an API key within your Pumble workspace administration panel. This token must be passed inside the HTTP header of every request as a bearer token.
It is **available on all** [**Pumble plans**](https://pumble.com/pricing)** to Owners, Admins, and Members**.
A Pumble workspace where you are allowed to install apps. The free Pumble plan is enough.
This addon lets you generate an API key that allows you to send messages, reactions, and more via simple HTTP requests.
It's mandatory to include the token (access token issued to user/bot) and x-app-token (app token issued to your app, prefixed with 'xpat-') headers in every request
Pumble maintains a native MCP (Model Context Protocol) server hosted directly at pumble.com, helping you connect your workspace to your AI agent of choice.
With the Pumble Model Context Protocol (MCP) server, you can connect third-party AI agents (e.g., Claude, Gemini, Codex) to Pumble
